subject: POC onboarding — org bootstrap, API keys, IP allowlist & VPC peering
messages:
From: Jane Park <jane.park@healthfast.io>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Dirk Mueller <dirk.mueller@aurora-med.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Dec 2029 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC kickoff & what we need from Redwood

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — team liked the latency numbers. We want to get a short POC in our staging environment next week. For the MAP and our security checklist the engineering and network teams asked for the following so we can schedule the testing window: 

- Redwood org creation and a service account for HealthFast (read/write to the POC tenant)
- API keys for the evaluation (scoped, ephemeral if possible)
- IP allowlist for outbound callbacks from our staging (we'll provide the CIDRs)
- VPC peering option or VPN details so our infra can reach the model endpoints in your dedicated sandbox

I attached a simple network diagram and our initial IP list. Can you confirm who on your side will own the peering setup and the expected lead time? We'd like to aim for a 5-business-day turnaround if possible.

Attachments: poa_network_diagram.pdf (diagram), hf_ip_allowlist_v1.csv (ip list)

Thanks,
Jane Park
Head of Integrations — HealthFast
[jane.park@healthfast.io]

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Jane Park <jane.park@healthfast.io>
Cc: Dir k Mueller <dirk.mueller@aurora-med.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Dec 2029 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff & what we need from Redwood

Hi Jane — great to hear the demo landed well.

We can support all four items. Quick answers below and a suggested mutual action plan (MAP) to hit a 5-business-day window:

1) Org & service account: I will create the HealthFast org namespace in our sandbox and provision a dedicated service account by EOD tomorrow (Dec 6). Please confirm the service account name you'd prefer (e.g., hf-poc-service-account).

2) API keys: we'll issue scoped API keys limited to the POC org with a 14-day TTL. If you want ephemeral rolling keys, we can enable that during the test — let me know.

3) IP allowlist: we received hf_ip_allowlist_v1.csv. Our infra team needs the allowlist in CIDR format per region (you have us listed as us-west1). We'll add those to the staging ingress ACL once confirmed.

4) VPC peering: Redwood supports two options: managed VPC peering (we handle the cloud-side config) or a customer-initiated VPN tunnel (you provide details). For a fast turn, I recommend managed peering — our network engineer (Ben Carter) will coordinate the routing and firewall rules.

Suggested MAP (compressed):
- Day 0 (Dec 5): HealthFast shares final CIDRs and preferred service-account name (action: HealthFast)
- Day 1 (Dec 6): Redwood creates org & service account; issues scoped API keys; schedule peering slot (action: Redwood — Aditya / Ben)
- Day 2 (Dec 7): Peering completed and IP allowlist applied; smoke test endpoints (action: Redwood / HealthFast)
- Day 3 (Dec 8): Validation run (sample requests, latency checks, auth verification) and quick QA report (action: both)

Acceptance criteria: endpoints reachable from your staging, keys validate, <200ms p95 for representative prompt, and no 401/403 errors during auth tests.

I'll loop in Ben and Soojin for tech ownership and to set the peering appointment.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Dec 2029 09:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: HealthFast POC — peering and creds coordination

Ben / Soojin —

Quick coordination note for HealthFast (HF-2029-71). Jane sent their CIDRs and asked for a 5-business-day turn. Core asks: org + service account, scoped API keys, IP allowlist, managed VPC peering preferred. I've already proposed the MAP to them.

Action items I want on your plates:
- Ben: own the managed peering slot. Can you confirm availability for Dec 7 midday PT? We'll need to: establish peering, verify route tables, and confirm firewall rules for outbound callbacks on ports 443 and 5222 (if they need websockets).
- Soojin: generate the scoped API keys under hf-poc-service-account and enable TTL = 14 days. Also prepare a short playbook with the exact header and auth examples that HealthFast can use for smoke tests (curl snippets).
- Marissa: please prepare the brief acceptance-runbook (one-pager) for CS and the customer that lists the exact tests and owner for each step.

Attached: internal checklist I'm proposing. If peering cannot be completed on Dec 7, we'll fall back to VPN instructions (Dirk mentioned they can accept a tunnel).

Thanks — please reply with confirmations and ETA.

-Aditya

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Jane Park <jane.park@healthfast.io>
Cc: Dirk Mueller <dirk.mueller@aurora-med.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 7 Dec 2029 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff & what we need from Redwood — confirmed MAP and timeline

Hi Jane — looping back with confirmed dates and owners. Quoting the key bits from earlier so everyone has a single view: 

On Thu, Dec 5, 2029 at 10:05 AM Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com> wrote:
> Suggested MAP (compressed):
> - Day 0 (Dec 5): HealthFast shares final CIDRs and preferred service-account name (action: HealthFast)
> - Day 1 (Dec 6): Redwood creates org & service account; issues scoped API keys; schedule peering slot (action: Redwood — Aditya / Ben)
> - Day 2 (Dec 7): Peering completed and IP allowlist applied; smoke test endpoints (action: Redwood / HealthFast)
> - Day 3 (Dec 8): Validation run (sample requests, latency checks, auth verification) and quick QA report (action: both)

Status update:
- HealthFast provided the final CIDRs (received Dec 5).
- We created org "healthfast-poc" and provisioned service account "hf-poc-service-account" (Dec 6) — Soojin created the scoped API keys and sent temporary credentials to Jane via secure link.
- Ben completed managed VPC peering this morning (Dec 7) between Redwood sandbox and HealthFast staging (routing and firewall rules verified).

Next steps & targets:
- Dec 7 (today): HealthFast to run smoke tests and confirm endpoints are reachable. See curl examples in the playbook Soojin attached.
- Dec 8: joint validation window 09:00–11:00 PT. Acceptance criteria: endpoints reachable, auth ok, p95 < 200ms on a 10-sample run, no auth errors.

If you run into any network errors please paste the curl request and exact error — we'll triage immediately.

Thanks everyone for the fast turnaround — talk tomorrow during the validation window.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: hf_acceptance_runbook.pdf]
